overall: The AG found the Board and its search subcommittee violated the OML by holding a Purpose 8 executive session on May 17 while the subcommittee included a board quorum, and ordered compliance and release of the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the library director search committee improperly met in executive session under Purpose 8 on May 17 because it included a quorum of the library board.
allegations.key_passage: Although we accept this explanation, we nonetheless find that because it contained a quorum of members of the Board, the Committee was not a preliminary screening committee under Purpose 8 and should not have met in executive session on May 17 to consider the applicants for library director.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the library board improperly convened in executive session on May 17 to consider applicants, since the committee doing so contained a board quorum.
allegations.key_passage: We also find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when a quorum acted as a preliminary screening committee and met in executive session on May 17 to consider library director applicants.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the board accepted only one final candidate for library director and did not hold public interviews; this was resolved in a prior determination.
allegations.key_passage: This allegation was resolved in Open Meeting Law determination letter OML 2018-142.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Board and the Committee.
The Committee must publicly release its May 17 executive session minutes without redacting or withholding any portion.
